children: According to Sina Finance, the United Nations Women agency said on October 2 that continued tensions in the Middle East have disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, pushed up global food prices, and put pressure on livelihoods.

The report said about 22 million more people worldwide could face food insecurity by the end of 2026, including 11.7 million women, or about 53% of the total. It also said people in Sudan, South Sudan, Yemen, Palestine, and Haiti face relatively severe food insecurity risks, with women affected more heavily. In Sudan, women account for nearly 56% of those who may face food insecurity. The report added that about 80% of women in Sudan, Egypt, Iraq, and Syria are outside the labor market, further increasing the risk of food insecurity for women.
The agency urged the parties involved to seek a diplomatic solution and ease regional tensions to promote peace and security in the region and internationally.

title: UN: Middle East Tensions Could Leave 22 Million More People Food Insecure
